decisions: Inspected all 13 worker merges, route passages and three substantive edits. C09 concerns available commitment leverage, not guaranteed compliance; agreement enforcement covers the whole agreement. Kept uncertainty and Chinese matching-cut disputes scoped. Local family/congregation risks do not require overall net manufacturing employment. Retired generic trade-as-acceptance.
source_context_read: Order and enforcement provisions, trade agreement clauses and monitoring statements, replacement-tariff announcements, China/USDA accounts, pass-through and input costs, hospital/water costs, and manufacturing null/offset evidence. Later replacement-policy observations are kept separate from the frozen comparison.

merges.decision: Direct bill text, checked word for word against the packet's bill text. No packet source disputes what the text says.

Follows directly from the termination law's text applied to taxes the order imposes under this emergency. The packet has no objection; an analysis of ending the same emergency reaches the same result.
Direct statutory text; the bill itself cites the provision. Whether this emergency was unlawful or harmful is a different question and is not part of this statement.
Direct legal text of the executive order, checked against the Federal Register copy. It is an order and not a statute; it is treated as verified legal text. No packet source disputes the wording.
Adequately sourced and not challenged by any retained response. The notes on slow price falls limit timing and size, and do not deny the direction of the effect.
Sourced to a water-industry analysis of the April 2 order and related warnings, with no retained response on this step. The delay is stated as a possibility, as in the source.
Sourced to hospital and device-maker statements, with no retained response on this step. The response to SEP_support_02 targets the later step to patient charges and stays local.
Direct text of the agreements, the framework statement and the September order. No packet source disputes these terms. Whether the terms give pressure for the promises is a separate statement.

Adequately sourced, and no retained response challenges this step. The April 2 order itself lists weak labor and environmental standards among the practices it addresses and allows lower rates if a partner remedies such practices. The September order ties relief to partners' commitments, and the deals contain these promises and allow action for not following 'a provision'. The Trade Representative says tariffs can go back into place. The remaining limits (not yet in force, no tariff action yet, general clause, other tools) do not deny that the tool existed on the comparison date. The response to SES_oppose_04 targets a later link and stays local.
Reported by several sources and in the official transcript, with no retained response. The limits below concern how much the pressure mattered, not whether it was used.

Substantive objection to this exact statement: officials announced they would replace the tariffs under other laws, so uncertainty might only move. The evidence points in both directions and no packet source measures uncertainty after such a repeal.

Substantive objection already attached to UNN_support_05: the cited Chinese cut came from negotiation, a repeal would be one-sided, and China's decision is its own. UNC_support_04's easing route uses the same May negotiated example.

substantive_edits.reason: Factual correction: 'when Congress voted' becomes 'when the Senate voted', because the packet text is the version engrossed in the Senate on October 30, 2025 (input bill record; bill text citation 1). Other edits are plain-language only; PRO and response meaning unchanged.

Factual precision: 'a route that skips required investigation' becomes 'a route that does not require an investigation', which is what CRS says (citation 24); Executive Order 14257 says the President received results of earlier investigations, and that note is routed to support (citations 10 and 24). Other edits are plain-language only.

Shorter sentences and plain terms; quotes, citations, conditions and meaning unchanged. Main review: The PRO removes this program as one documented source of shocks. The reply asks for an end to sudden tariff news generally. Announced replacement powers do not rebut that narrower source-removal claim; their timing and reach remain relevant to strength.

Substantive placement: the price-protection and American Giant premise moves from the retired Main effect panel into the PRO, because the response answers that premise and the panel no longer appears. No new source; the quotes are from the input Main effect (citations 25 and 26). Other edits are plain-language only.

limits: Targeted source context, not exhaustive independent verification of all sources.
